title: Weather: does the market add to a public forecast?
finding: On 119 held-out NYC days in July–December 2025, normalized Kalshi prices had 10.4% lower mean binary Brier error than a simple prior-error-calibrated NBM baseline. The training-fitted combination did not clearly improve on the market. This is one city and one deliberately limited public benchmark.

methods: Unit: a complete six-contract Kalshi NYC daily-high ladder, equal weight per day. The daily score is the average of six binary Brier scores, (p − outcome)². Lower is better; this is not temperature RMSE or percent-correct.

Comparison cutoff: civil midnight America/New_York on the event date derived from the ticker (04Z during daylight saving time; 05Z otherwise), not administrative settlement time. All retained price observations precede that cutoff and are no more than six hours old. NWS CLI outcomes instead cover midnight-to-midnight local STANDARD time: 05Z to next-day 05Z year round in NYC. Thus the comparison is one hour before the CLI day starts during daylight saving time, and at its start otherwise; it does not include observations from the target CLI day.

Require four contiguous two-degree interior intervals and two complementary tails; retain ladders with price sums from 0.7 to 1.3 and one winning outcome. Normalize all six YES trade prices by their sum. This removes ladder incoherence, not a proven fee or bid/ask adjustment.

Public input: archived as-issued NOAA NBM NBS guidance at KNYC, accessed through Iowa Environmental Mesonet. Select the latest model runtime at least three hours before the comparison cutoff; actual dissemination timestamps are unavailable.

NBM point approximation is the larger of its TXN maximum (12Z through 06Z, labeled at 00Z) and three-hourly TMP forecasts inside the civil calendar day. The settlement target is the NWS CLI local-standard-time day (05Z to next-day 05Z), not the civil day; this forecast construction only approximates that target window.

Convert that point forecast to six probabilities using its empirical errors on the preceding 180 calendar days, excluding the immediately preceding day and requiring at least 60 observations. Errors use archived NWS Central Park CLI highs. No current or future outcome enters a forecast.

Fit one convex market/public mixing weight by minimizing Brier error on January–June 2025 only. Freeze the weight and score July–December 2025. Residual calibration updates with prior available days; there is no test-period weight tuning.
Uncertainty: 5,000 bootstrap resamples of 27 fixed seven-day calendar clusters in the held-out sample; this preserves dependence within a week, not all longer weather patterns. Seed 64119.

Official sample rule checks confirm Central Park NWS daily climatological settlement, B59.5 = 59–60°F, T55 = below 55°F, and T62 = above 62°F. All retained ladders must follow the same contiguous suffix geometry. Outcome-vs-CLI disagreements are retained and disclosed.
limitations: One city, 2025 only, and a simple empirical-error NBM model. It is not the full NBM distribution or a best-of-public-model ensemble, and cannot establish superiority over the best public forecasting system.

The NBM TXN window extends one hour beyond the CLI day ending at 05Z and omits early hours; three-hourly TMP cannot reconstruct every hourly extreme. Civil-midnight comparison time is additionally one hour before the CLI observation day starts during daylight saving time. A forecast ensemble matched exactly to the 05Z–05Z observation window is the next stronger benchmark.

The three-hour availability buffer is an assumption; archived model runtime is not archived public posting time. The six-hour-buffer sensitivity uses older guidance and does not identify minute-by-minute price discovery.

Prices are last trades from the existing one-day panel, not simultaneous quotes, executable prices, or forecast-time snapshots. Freshness screening can favor active markets, and normalizing a ladder is not a transaction-cost estimate.
Residual calibration uses the currently archived CLI reports with a two-day delay. Later corrections to old reports are not reconstructed as initially published.
The temporal holdout is a reproducible development/test split, not a preregistered prospective study. Fixed-week bootstrap intervals do not remove all seasonal dependence or model-selection risk.

The related 2026 preprint already studies a broader multi-city/public-model comparison; this addition is an independently computed, narrower probability-score benchmark, not a claim of novel discovery.
